template: On dashboard '{{v1}}' (uid {{v3}}): set the dashboard time range to 'Last 6 hours' (via the top time picker), add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard (via Dashboard settings → General → Tags), and when saving, make sure the save dialog option to update the dashboard's default time range IS ticked so the 6-hour range persists in the saved dashboard. Save. Then verify persistence: reload the page, open Dashboard settings → General and confirm the tag 'bench' is listed, and confirm the saved default time range is Last 6 hours (e.g. by opening a fresh new browser tab to the dashboard and checking the time picker, or checking the settings' time range). Report what you observe.

reportTemplate.summary: On dashboard '{{v1}}' (uid {{v3}}) I set the top time picker to 'Last 6 hours', added the tag 'bench' via Edit → Settings → General → Tags → Add, and saved via Edit → Save dashboard with the drawer's 'Update default time range' option ticked (the [state] diff showed the checkbox [checked] and the Save button going from [disabled] to enabled). Because the stored default already matched 6h, I first ran a discriminating test: saving with the same box ticked while the range was 'Last 5 minutes' made the plain URL show 'Last 5 minutes', proving the tick really rewrites the persisted default; I then set the picker back to 'Last 6 hours' and saved with the tick again. After hard reloading the parameterless URL /d/{{v3}}/{{v4}}, the time picker reads 'Last 6 hours', and reopening Settings → General shows the tag 'bench' listed (chip with a 'Remove "bench" tag' button). (saved_default_time_range: plain, parameterless URL reload showed 'Last 6 hours')

values.discriminating_test: saving with the tick at 'Last 5 minutes' made the plain URL show 'Last 5 minutes', proving the ticked option rewrites the persisted default; re-saving with the tick at 6h restored 'Last 6 hours'
